## Steps

1. **Entry check.** Run `uv run rmf status <run>`: P-14 is the next action, and
   P-3, P-13 are done or out of scope.
   Entry criteria (from `framework/tasks/P.yaml`):
   - Assets, boundary and information life cycle documented (P-10, P-11, P-13); threat information available.
   If one is not met, stop and journal a NOTE (`00-run-protocol.md`, stop conditions). Why:
   the task builds on those results, and working around a gap leaves claims nobody can
   trace.
2. **Read the inputs** listed in `## Inputs`, and the passages in `## Citations` that say
   what P-14 must achieve. The purpose in the header states the outcome.
   P-14 feeds MS-A (Milestone A, milestone), RV-SRR (System Requirements Review, review); what it
   records must be ready for those events.
   Why: the playbook is generic, so the inputs and the cited text set the content.
3. **Interview** following `_shared/interviewing.md` (and `_shared/hybrid-mode.md` in a
   `hybrid` run). Start with the responsible (R) personas in `## Interviews`. Take the
   questions from each persona card's `## Question bank by step` for step P
   (Prepare) and point them at what the exit criteria in `## Done when` need and the
   inputs leave open.
   Write at least 1 interview file(s) with `task: P-14`.
   Why: answers are the evidence that artifacts cite (`INT-###.A#`).
4. **Write the outputs** in `## Outputs`, each file whole (INV-8), every claim traced per
   `_shared/tagging-and-traceability.md`:
   - **ART-RA** (System risk assessment): System-level security and privacy risk assessment, updated as the system and threat change.
     Read `templates/artifacts/ART-RA.md`, replace every `<<FILL: ...>>` placeholder, delete the template
     comment, and write `artifacts/ART-RA.md` with `produced_by_task: P-14` and
     `touched_by: [P-14]`.
     Write `artifacts/data/ra.yaml` whole (schema `framework/schema/ra.schema.json`, template `templates/data/ra.yaml`); summarize its records in the Markdown by ID instead of copying them.
     Write `artifacts/data/protection.yaml` whole (schema `framework/schema/protection.schema.json`, template `templates/data/protection.yaml`); summarize its records in the Markdown by ID instead of copying them.
     Write `artifacts/data/st-protection.yaml` whole (schema `framework/schema/st-protection.schema.json`, template `templates/data/st-protection.yaml`); summarize its records in the Markdown by ID instead of copying them.
     Write `artifacts/data/scrm.yaml` whole (schema `framework/schema/scrm.schema.json`, template `templates/data/scrm.yaml`); summarize its records in the Markdown by ID instead of copying them.
   - **ART-PIA** (Privacy impact assessment): The DD Form 2930 (or 2930A) PIA of a system processing PII, its coordination, reviews and final approval, its submission to the DoD CIO and the publication of section 1; or, for a system needing no PIA, the determination that says why.
     Read `templates/artifacts/ART-PIA.md`, replace every `<<FILL: ...>>` placeholder, delete the template
     comment, and write `artifacts/ART-PIA.md` with `produced_by_task: P-14` and
     `touched_by: [P-14]`.
     Write `artifacts/data/pia.yaml` whole (schema `framework/schema/pia.schema.json`, template `templates/data/pia.yaml`); summarize its records in the Markdown by ID instead of copying them.
   Why: `rmf status` counts P-14 done only when every output lists it in `touched_by`.
5. **Leave `facts.yaml` alone.** P-14 writes no facts (INV-4).
6. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task P-14`,
   until 0 errors (INV-6).
7. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT (`## Journal and lessons`).

## Facts

P-14 writes no facts.

## Done when

- A system-level risk assessment is completed or an existing risk assessment is updated (DoDI 8510.01 Table 1 outcome).
- ART-RA records threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact and the resulting risks.
- artifacts/data/ra.yaml states the purpose, scope, assumptions, constraints, dated information sources, risk model, analytic approach and risk tolerance, rates each threat source, threat event, vulnerability and predisposing condition, and holds the risk of each connection, external provider and supplier, the priority order and to whom the results are communicated (SRA-001 to SRA-003).
- ART-RA identifies the system elements and interfaces that need specific attention in test events, for the cybersecurity strategy and the TEMP.
- For a system processing PII, artifacts/data/ra.yaml `privacy` assesses the nature of the processing and its impact on individuals and evaluates each legal and policy privacy requirement, OMB A-130 among them, with what the privacy baseline leaves unmet (PRIV-007); where P-12 found a PIA required, artifacts/data/pia.yaml holds it on DD Form 2930 (2930A when adapted), coordinated through the ISSM, the privacy representative and the records office, reviewed by PER-CISO and PER-PRIV and approved by PER-CIO or the reviewing official (PRIV-002, PRIV-003).
- ra.yaml components records each third-party and open-source software component with the six risk factors of DoWI 8430.01 3.5.i.(2), the further governance, community and license review of a non-trivial open-source component, and any independent third-party validation of a commercial product (SWA-002); ra.yaml ai_capabilities records each AI-enabled capability's use case risk, benchmarks, verification before deployment, monitoring and bias handling (DoWI 8430.01 3.6.e).
- protection.yaml records the PPP the run read with its approval at each decision point passed, its critical items with their threats, vulnerabilities and countermeasures, exportability, anti-tamper, updates and transition (PPROT-001, PPROT-002); the TAPPs, horizontal protection guidance and S&T protection plan read (PPROT-003); and the security technical risks from the SEP and ITRAs with the reviews that assess them (PPROT-005).
- artifacts/data/scrm.yaml records the criticality analysis and TSN practices, a supplier for every inventory item tied to its ra.yaml supply chain record, the threat analysis, and an assessment of every critical supplier covering each Table 28 factor, with its SCRSS level, escalation and FASC sharing (SCRM-001 to SCRM-006).
- `artifacts/ART-RA.md` lists P-14 in `touched_by` and has `produced_by_task: P-14`.
- `artifacts/ART-PIA.md` lists P-14 in `touched_by` and has `produced_by_task: P-14`.
- At least 1 interview(s) with `task: P-14`.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task P-14` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task P-14`, naming what the outputs now hold.
- If the work shows that P-3 (Risk Assessment—Organization) got something wrong, do not change that task's
  outputs here: journal a NOTE naming the file and the evidence. P-14 feeds back to P-3.
- A fix that took more than one `rmf check` round gets a RETRY entry and a lesson
  (`_shared/journaling-and-lessons.md`).
